message.content:
Review the changes on the current git branch `feature/aim-styles-preview` against its base `feature/player-journal`. This is a C++ raylib game. Run:

  cd /Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs
  git diff feature/player-journal...HEAD

The branch has three commits implementing three GitHub issues:
- #91 fix(combat): derive gun aim from one shared lookDirection(yaw,pitch) used by both the camera and the weapon; spawn the projectile from eye height along the full 3D aim (was: yaw-only horizontal aim from the feet). New Math.hpp helpers lookDirection + kEyeHeight; World::projectiles() accessor; tests in tests/test_aim.cpp.
- #92 feat(creator): more style-tagged character parts + palettes in CharacterParts.cpp with renderer recipes in RaylibRenderer.cpp drawCompositeCharacter.
- #93 feat(creator): replace the creator preview auto-spin with a two-state model in main.cpp (drag/keys rotate; idle-return-to-front) + Menu::pointOverInteractive; shortestAngleDelta in Math.hpp.

Focus on correctness bugs, not style. Specifically check:
1. The aim math: does lookDirection's convention actually match the camera basis it replaced in RaylibRenderer::beginFrame? Could the projectile hit-detection (XZ distance + [0,kNpcHeight] band in World::tickProjectiles) break now that shots travel in 3D from eye height instead of horizontally from the feet?
2. Any new part in CharacterParts.cpp that could fail style-compatibility assembly or collide with an existing id, and whether every new part actually renders (bespoke recipe or generic fallback).
3. The preview rotation state machine: is there ANY code path where rotation advances without player input or the idle-return? Off-by-one / wrap issues in shortestAngleDelta? Does the drag-vs-click gate (pointOverInteractive) actually prevent a control-click from also rotating?

The full suite passes (165 cases / 2343 assertions). Report only real issues with file:line and a concrete failure scenario; if you find nothing substantive, say so plainly. Do not modify files.

content.text:
Review complete. I examined the full diff (`feature/player-journal...HEAD`, 3 commits), plus `World.cpp/hpp`, `Math.hpp`, `CharacterParts.cpp`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp` (drawCompositeCharacter + beginFrame), `Menu.cpp/hpp`, and the preview block in `main.cpp`.

## Verified sound (the three focus questions)

1. **Aim math (#91)** — `lookDirection` at `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/src/core/Math.hpp:87` is byte-for-byte the basis it replaced in `RaylibRenderer::beginFrame` (`sin(yaw)cos(pitch), sin(pitch), cos(yaw)cos(pitch)`), and spawn height (`player_.position + kEyeHeight`, World.cpp:40) matches the camera (`pose.position.y + kEyeHeight`). Zero-pitch equals `flatForward`, so aim/movement parity holds. Hit detection survives the 3D change: spawn y = 1.7 sits inside the `[0, 1.8]` band, the per-frame step (40 u/s → ~0.67 u at 60 fps) can't tunnel vertically through a 1.8-tall band even at the ±75° pitch clamp, and crosshair-on-target shots stay in band at the target's XZ by construction.
2. **Parts (#92)** — no id collisions (the `hair_mohawk` test collision was correctly renamed to `hair_dreadlocks`); every category keeps ≥1 option in both style families plus "any", so `randomizeLook`'s `options[rng.pick(...)]` can't index an empty vector; all 8 new parts render — bespoke recipes for `body_slim`/`head_oval`/`hair_pony`/`hair_mohawk`, the shared two-pupil Eyes branch for `eyes_round`/`eyes_happy` (dx math checks out), generic box fallback for `body_bulk`/`head_tall` with correct skin/outfit color routing.
3. **Preview (#93)** — no autonomous-spin path exists; rotation only changes under key/drag input or the post-timeout ease. `shortestAngleDelta` correctly handles negative `fmod` and stays in [-180, 180]. The ease is frame-rate independent (`1 - exp(-rate·dt)`). `test_aim.cpp` needs no build registration (tests/Makefile globs `test_*.cpp`).

## Issues

**HIGH**

- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/src/app/main.cpp:1025-1027` — the drag-vs-click gate is evaluated per frame against the *current* mouse position instead of being latched at press, so it does not fully prevent a control-click from rotating. Failure scenario: press a part cycler `[<]`/`[>]` (44×40 px rect; the click fires on `IsMouseButtonPressed` in Menu.cpp:286-291), keep the button held, and flick the mouse off the rect — a natural click gesture. `pointOverInteractive` now returns false while the button is still down, so `GetMouseDelta().x` spins the preview. This directly violates the documented contract in `Menu.hpp:86-90` ("clicking a cycler/button never spins the preview"). The inverse also fails: a legitimate drag started over empty space stalls every time the cursor crosses any hit rect mid-drag. Fix: on `IsMouseButtonPressed`, latch `bool draggingPreview = !menu.pointOverInteractive(GetMousePosition())` and gate rotation on that latch until release.

**MEDIUM**

- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/src/app/main.cpp:1029-1038` — holding the drag button on the preview with the mouse stationary counts as idle (`rotateInput == 0`), so after 2.5 s of holding still the figure starts easing back to front while the player is "grabbing" it. Failure scenario: drag to the back of the character, hold to inspect — it rotates away under the cursor. Fix: also reset `previewIdleSeconds` while an eligible drag button is down (folds into the HIGH item's latch).

**LOW**

- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/src/app/main.cpp:1023-1024` — Left/Right rotate the preview even while a persona text field has focus (`editingField_ != 0`). No conflict today (fields are append/backspace only), but there's no focus gate; if field cursor navigation is ever added, arrows will double-handle. Consider exposing a `menu.isEditingText()` guard.
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/src/core/World.cpp:70,89` — downward shots that miss now continue below y=0, flying underground for the rest of `maxLifetime` (nothing culls on ground contact; the band check just skips them). Harmless while projectiles aren't rendered, but it becomes visible underground tracers the day a projectile renderer lands. Cheap fix: erase when `position.y < 0 && direction.y < 0`.
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs/src/app/RaylibRenderer.cpp:367-371` — `head_oval` uses a non-uniform `rlScalef` on a sphere, which skews lighting normals (raylib doesn't renormalize). Purely cosmetic shading artifact; fine to ship.

Pre-existing, not from this branch: stale `// TODO(combat): implement these` at `World.hpp:96` (they are implemented) — worth deleting sometime given the no-TODOs rule.

Done well: extracting `kEyeHeight` and `lookDirection` into Math.hpp genuinely closes the camera/weapon divergence class rather than patching one call site; the `hair_mohawk` test fixup shows the catalog change was cross-checked against the suite; the generic-box render fallback plus the "any" style tags make the parts addition safely additive; and the test coverage for both the convention and the per-shot derivation is exactly the right regression net for #91. The one substantive problem is the unlatched drag gate.
